q: Under the Formula in Sec. 4.1, reimbursable expenses (R) for transportation, per diem, and housing/living allowance of local consultants and technical staff apply when they are assigned to places located how far from the Architect's area of operation?
o: Over 100 km
Any distance outside Metro Manila
Over 50 km
Over 200 km
AVISALA
n: The Formula defines R as including such allowances for consultants and technical staff "if assigned to places over 100 km. from the area of operation of the Architect." (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.1 (Formula))

q: An Architect engaged for Pre-Design Services brings in a structural engineering firm to provide specialized input, formalized under the extended terms of the Owner-Architect Agreement. Which Sec. 3.2 manner of rendering services does this illustrate?
o: Through the Architect's Own Staff (Sec. 3.2.2)
Promotional Services (Sec. 2.12)
As an individual Architect (Sec. 3.2.1)
By Association, Consultation, or Networking (Sec. 3.2.3)
n: Sec. 3.2.3 describes consultation between an Architect and a firm of other disciplines under the extended terms of the Owner-Architect Agreement as association/consultation/networking. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 3.2.3)

q: Overall, which phase of an architectural project's life cycle does SPP Document 201 govern, based on the range of services it enumerates (from consultation and feasibility studies through design brief preparation)?
o: The Pre-Design phase — the stage before actual architectural design/schematic work begins, in which problems are identified and initially conceptualized
The building permit processing phase exclusively
The construction supervision phase
The post-occupancy evaluation phase
n: Sec. 2 describes Pre-Design Services as covering services "ranging from initial problem identification to activities that would allow the Architect to initially conceptualize" solutions — i.e., the stage preceding actual design. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2)

q: Professional Fee Plus Expenses (Sec. 4.2) is most frequently used in what situation, and what must be agreed upon to set an equitable fee?
o: It requires no agreement on scope, only on the final deadline
Where there is a continuing relationship involving a series of projects; the general scope of work must be agreed upon
Only for projects under government contract
Only for one-time, single-building residential projects
n: Sec. 4.2 states this method is frequently used where there is a continuing relationship involving a series of projects, establishing a fixed sum above reimbursement for technical time and overhead, requiring agreement on the general scope of work. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.2)

q: SPP Document 201 is described as forming part of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of which law?
o: P.D. 1096 (National Building Code)
R.A. No. 386 (Civil Code)
n: The document header states SPP Doc. 201 on Pre-Design Services is "Part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266," the Architecture Act. (Source: SPP Document 201, Title/Header)

q: Architectural Programming (Sec. 2.7) is best described as:
o: A purely cost-based accounting exercise
An analytical problem-seeking process leading to identification of horizontal and vertical requirements, incorporating a space program with characterizations such as ambiance and cost range
The literal preparation of construction schedules/Gantt charts
The final signing and sealing of architectural plans
n: Sec. 2.7 describes Architectural Programming as an analytical problem-seeking process identifying horizontal and vertical requirements and incorporating a space program with characterizations like ambiance and cost range. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.7)

q: A Client asks the Architect, purely as agent, to conduct an ocular inspection of a possible project site and attend an out-of-town investment meeting on the Client's behalf. Under Sec. 4.4, how may the Architect be compensated for this personal-time work?
o: On a per diem and honorarium basis plus out-of-pocket expenses such as travel, accommodations, and subsistence
Only through a Lump Sum fee agreed at the start of the entire project
Only through the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method
The Architect may not accept compensation for such activities
n: Sec. 4.4 covers activities like project-related meetings/trips, ocular site inspections, and conferring on prospective investments, compensable on a per diem and honorarium basis plus out-of-pocket expenses (travel, accommodations, subsistence). (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.4)

q: Which of the following is NOT listed under the Scope of Pre-Design Services in SPP Doc. 201, Sec. 2?
o: Value management
Construction supervision
Feasibility studies
Architectural programming
n: Sec. 2 lists consultation, pre-feasibility and feasibility studies, site selection/analysis, site utilization and land-use studies, architectural research, architectural programming, space planning, space management studies, value management, design brief preparation, and promotional services — construction supervision is a separate SPP document, not a Pre-Design service. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2)

q: SPP Doc. 201, Sec. 3.2 recognizes how many manners in which an Architect can render Pre-Design services, and what are they?
o: One: only through the Architect's own staff
Three: as an individual Architect, through the Architect's own staff, or by association/consultation/networking
Two: as an individual Architect or as a government employee
Four, including outsourcing entirely to a foreign firm
n: Sec. 3.2 lists three manners: (3.2.1) as an individual Architect, (3.2.2) through the Architect's own staff, and (3.2.3) by association, consultation, or networking. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 3.2)

q: The Client requested 8 sets of the feasibility report. Under the Formula's definition of R, how many of those sets would be billable as an extra reimbursable cost item?
o: 5 sets
8 sets
3 sets
0 sets
n: R includes the "cost of printing of extra set of drawings, reports, maps, contract documents, etc. over the five (5) copies submitted to the Client." Since 5 copies are standard, 8 - 5 = 3 extra sets are billable as reimbursable cost. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.1 (Formula, definition of R))
scenario: An Architect renders Pre-Design Services (a feasibility study) for a Client under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method. The Architect logged 40 hours at ₱800/hour, one Consultant logged 20 hours at ₱1,000/hour, and Technical Staff logged 60 hours at ₱300/hour. The firm applies a multiplier of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Because the project site is 150 km from the Architect's area of operation, the Consultant and Technical Staff incurred reimbursable travel and lodging expenses totaling ₱15,000. The Client also requested 8 sets of the feasibility report instead of the standard number of copies submitted to the Client.

q: According to the Introduction of SPP Doc. 201, why must the Architect expand his/her basic services over time even though those services have remained relatively unchanged?
o: Because the Professional Regulatory Board requires new services every five years
Because UAP membership dues fund new service categories
In response to increasing Client demands, evolving standards of professional practice, advancing technology, and new laws
Because foreign architects are barred from all but expanded services
n: Sec. 1.1 states the Architect must expand services in response to increasing Client demands, evolving standards of regulated professional practice, advancing technology, and new laws. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 1.1)

q: An Architect meets with a prospective Client, gives written advice on a contemplated project, but the Client ultimately decides not to proceed. Under SPP Doc. 201, how should this engagement be characterized?
o: As an invalid engagement, since no fee can attach unless the project proceeds
As Consultation, a valid Pre-Design service rendered regardless of the project's outcome
As a violation of the Code of Ethics
As Architectural Research only
n: Consultation (Sec. 2.1) covers oral/written advice, conferences, and evaluations, and is a valid, compensable Pre-Design service whether or not the Client pursues the project. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.1)

q: The Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method (Sec. 4.1) is applicable only to what kind of work, and why?
o: Non-creative work such as accounting, secretarial, research, data gathering, and report preparation — because the value of creative design cannot be measured by time spent
Only work performed by foreign consultants
Purely creative design work, since it best rewards design talent
Construction supervision only
n: Sec. 4.1 states this cost-based method applies only to non-creative work (accounting, secretarial, research, data gathering, report preparation) since creative design's value cannot be measured by time spent. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.1)

q: How do Feasibility Studies (Sec. 2.3) differ from Pre-Feasibility Studies in terms of data requirements?
o: Both rely exclusively on secondary data
Feasibility Studies require primary data gathering and analysis to determine project viability, going beyond the secondary-data basis of Pre-Feasibility Studies
Feasibility Studies use only secondary data, while Pre-Feasibility Studies require primary data
Feasibility Studies do not consider present or future trends
n: Sec. 2.3 states Feasibility Studies involve detailed analysis based on the pre-feasibility studies and require primary data gathering and analysis to determine viability and forecast performance over time. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.3)

q: Per Sec. 3.1, after the initial meeting/conversation/correspondence with the Client, what must the Architect submit before rendering Pre-Design Services, and what must it state?
o: A proposal for pre-design services, stating the Scope of Work, Manner of Payment, Owner's Responsibilities, and Other Conditions of Services
Only a verbal confirmation of the fee
A notarized deed of sale for the property
A signed as-built survey of the site
n: Sec. 3.1 requires the Architect to submit a proposal for pre-design services stating the Scope of Work (3.1.1), Manner of Payment (3.1.2), Owner's Responsibilities, and Other Conditions of Services (3.1.3-3.1.4). (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 3.1)

q: What is the Total Cost of Service that should be charged to the Client (Total Cost = Fee + R)?
n: Total Cost of Service = Fee + R = ₱140,000 + ₱15,000 (reimbursable travel/lodging) = ₱155,000. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.1 (Formula: Total Cost of Service = Fee + R))
scenario: An Architect renders Pre-Design Services (a feasibility study) for a Client under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method. The Architect logged 40 hours at ₱800/hour, one Consultant logged 20 hours at ₱1,000/hour, and Technical Staff logged 60 hours at ₱300/hour. The firm applies a multiplier of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Because the project site is 150 km from the Architect's area of operation, the Consultant and Technical Staff incurred reimbursable travel and lodging expenses totaling ₱15,000. The Client also requested 8 sets of the feasibility report instead of the standard number of copies submitted to the Client.

q: What does Architectural Research (Sec. 2.6) involve?
o: Cost estimation using only historical bid data
Only literature review with no primary data collection
The conduct of primary and secondary research and assembled facts used as the basis for conclusions
Structural computations for the proposed building
n: Sec. 2.6 defines Architectural Research as the conduct of primary and secondary researches and assembled facts used as basis for conclusion. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.6)

q: What does Site Selection and Analysis (Sec. 2.4) entail?
o: Drafting the building permit application
Formulating site criteria and assisting the Client in site evaluation/analysis to determine the most appropriate site(s) for the project or building program
Negotiating the purchase price of the site on the Client's behalf as broker
Preparing the final architectural design for a chosen site
n: Sec. 2.4 defines Site Selection and Analysis as formulating site criteria and assisting the Client in evaluating and analyzing sites to determine the most appropriate one. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.4)

q: Applying Fee = Direct Cost x M, what is the Architect's Fee at the firm's stated multiplier?
n: Fee = Direct Cost x M = ₱70,000 x 2.0 = ₱140,000. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.1 (Formula: Fee = Direct Cost x M))
scenario: An Architect renders Pre-Design Services (a feasibility study) for a Client under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method. The Architect logged 40 hours at ₱800/hour, one Consultant logged 20 hours at ₱1,000/hour, and Technical Staff logged 60 hours at ₱300/hour. The firm applies a multiplier of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Because the project site is 150 km from the Architect's area of operation, the Consultant and Technical Staff incurred reimbursable travel and lodging expenses totaling ₱15,000. The Client also requested 8 sets of the feasibility report instead of the standard number of copies submitted to the Client.

q: Which data-gathering methods are cited under Space Planning (Sec. 2.8)?
o: Only satellite imagery
Interviews, consultations, focus group discussions (FGDs), space planning surveys, and space audits, followed by analyses such as spatial layouts and stacking concepts
Only financial audits
Only building code review
n: Sec. 2.8 states Space Planning is done through primary data gathering (interviews, consultations, interfaces, FGDs, space planning surveys, space audits) and subsequent analyses such as spatial layouts with stacking concepts. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.8)

q: Space Management Studies (Sec. 2.9) analyze space requirements based on what basis, and what do they produce?
o: Based on the organizational structure and functional set-up, pinpointing linkages/interaction of spaces; the resulting space program becomes the basis for the architectural plan/design
Based solely on the Client's personal aesthetic taste
Based on the site's topography alone
Based on the contractor's construction sequencing
n: Sec. 2.9 states the analysis is based on organizational structure and functional set-up, pinpointing linkages and interaction of spaces, with the resulting space program serving as basis for the architectural plan/design. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.9)

q: If the firm had instead applied the lowest end of the allowable multiplier range (1.5) rather than 2.0, what would the resulting Fee have been?
n: Fee = Direct Cost x M = ₱70,000 x 1.5 = ₱105,000, since Sec. 4.1 allows the multiplier to range from 1.5 to 2.5. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.1 (multiplier range 1.5-2.5))
scenario: An Architect renders Pre-Design Services (a feasibility study) for a Client under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method. The Architect logged 40 hours at ₱800/hour, one Consultant logged 20 hours at ₱1,000/hour, and Technical Staff logged 60 hours at ₱300/hour. The firm applies a multiplier of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Because the project site is 150 km from the Architect's area of operation, the Consultant and Technical Staff incurred reimbursable travel and lodging expenses totaling ₱15,000. The Client also requested 8 sets of the feasibility report instead of the standard number of copies submitted to the Client.

q: A prospective Client asks an Architect whether it truly matters if the Architect is engaged only after a project's basic parameters have already been fixed by others. Based on Sec. 1.2, what should the Architect explain?
o: Only foreign consultants should be engaged at the earliest stage
It makes no difference, since Pre-Design Services can only be rendered after design begins

Involving the Architect at the earliest stages is most advantageous, since an experienced Architect can provide objective project analysis and optimize building needs against available resources and constraints
Early involvement is discouraged because it increases the Architect's liability
n: Sec. 1.2 states it is most advantageous to the Client to involve the Architect at the earliest stages, since a suitably experienced Architect provides objective project analysis and optimizes building needs versus resources and constraints. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 1.2)

q: Site Utilization and Land-Use Studies (Sec. 2.5) analyze which factors?
o: Only the aesthetic preferences of the Client
Only the structural bearing capacity of the soil
The site's development potentials through proper land utilization, covering the site's context, its surrounding environment, and applicable development controls
Only the boundaries and title of the site
n: Sec. 2.5 states the analysis identifies the site's development potentials through proper land utilization, covering the site's context, its surrounding environment, and applicable development controls. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.5)

q: As a general/overall matter, why does SPP Doc. 201 emphasize that the Architect must submit a written proposal (Sec. 3.1) before commencing Pre-Design Services, rather than simply beginning work after a verbal request?
o: Because only written proposals may be submitted to the PRC Board of Architecture
Because SPP Doc. 201 requires notarization of every architectural service, however small

To ensure the Scope of Work, Manner of Payment, Owner's Responsibilities, and Other Conditions of Services are clearly established between Architect and Client from the outset, avoiding later disputes
Because verbal agreements are void under the Civil Code
n: Sec. 3.1 requires a proposal stating scope, payment terms, Owner's responsibilities, and other conditions precisely so that the terms of engagement are clear before pre-design work begins, consistent with the document's overall aim of professionalizing the Architect-Client relationship from the earliest stage. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 3.1)

q: A government agency asks its engaged Architect to also produce and coordinate activities to build public acceptance for a proposed project. Under Sec. 2.12 (Promotional Services), what must the Architect maintain while performing this role?
o: Exclusive control over the project's final budget approval
A separate business permit as an advertising agency
Strict silence and non-involvement with governing agencies
His/her professional status as the representative (agent) of the Owner, throughout all such promotional activities
n: Sec. 2.12 states that in acting as agent of the Owner for promotional activities, the Architect must maintain his/her professional status as the representative of the Owner. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.12)

q: Lump Sum or Fixed Fee (Sec. 4.3) is described as a method that may be applied to which type of project, and why?
o: Only interior design projects
Only private residential projects, since they are simplest to scope
Government projects, since they entail more paperwork and time-consuming efforts
Projects with no defined scope of work
n: Sec. 4.3 states this method may be applied to government projects since they entail more paper work and time-consuming efforts. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.3)

q: Under Sec. 4.1, the multiplier applied to technical service costs (to cover overhead and profit) ranges over what values, and what factors affect where in that range it falls?
o: 1.5 to 2.5, depending on the office set-up, overhead, experience of the Architect, and the complexity of the Project
2.5 to 4.0, depending only on the Client's budget
There is no defined range; it is negotiated case by case with no guidance
1.0 to 1.2, fixed regardless of project complexity
n: Sec. 4.1 (and the Formula section) states the multiplier ranges from 1.5 to 2.5 depending on the office set-up, overhead, experience of the Architect, and complexity of the Project. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.1)

q: What is the stated goal of Value Management (Sec. 2.10)?
o: To achieve an unimpaired program at minimum cost, such that the value-managed plan/design/system still satisfies the same performance criteria as costlier alternatives
To maximize the Architect's professional fee
To eliminate the need for a feasibility study
To reduce the program's scope regardless of performance impact
n: Sec. 2.10 states the goal of value management is an unimpaired program at minimum cost, with the value-managed result still meeting the same performance criteria as costlier alternatives. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.10)

q: SPP Document 201 governs which set of architectural services, and what document does it replace?
o: Design Services; replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 202
Post-Construction Services; replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 401
Construction Supervision; replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 301
Pre-Design Services; replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 201
n: SPP Document 201, part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266, covers Pre-Design Services and expressly replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 201. (Source: SPP Document 201, Title/Header)

q: An Architect's proposal to a Client for Pre-Design Services describes the Scope of Work and the fee, but says nothing about what the Owner must furnish or any other conditions. Under Sec. 3.1, what is missing from this proposal?
o: A construction timeline, which SPP Doc. 201 requires in every proposal
A statement of the Owner's Responsibilities and Other Conditions of Services
Nothing; the proposal is already complete
The Architect's PRC license number only
n: Sec. 3.1 requires the proposal to also state the Owner's Responsibilities and Other Conditions of Services, in addition to Scope of Work and Manner of Payment. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 3.1)

q: What does Sec. 4.5 (Mixed Methods of Compensation) provide regarding the choice of compensation method for a given project?
o: Only one method may ever be used per project, with no exceptions
The SPP allows for more than one method of compensation on a project, with each project examined to determine the most appropriate and equitable method
The Client alone decides the method, with no input from the Architect
Mixed methods are prohibited to avoid billing confusion
n: Sec. 4.5 states the SPP provides for more than one method of compensation on a project, and each project should be examined to determine the most appropriate and equitable method. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.5)

q: Before agreeing with a Client to use the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method, what must the Architect disclose?
o: The Architect's personal income tax return
The rate of professionals/personnel to be assigned to the Project and the multiplier to be applied
Only the total project cost estimate
Nothing; disclosure is optional under this method
n: Sec. 4.1 requires the Architect to make known to the Client, at the start of the commission, the rate of professionals/personnel assigned and the multiplier to be applied, before agreeing on this method. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.1)

q: According to Sec. 4, what is the Architect's compensation fundamentally based on?
o: Solely the physical size of the Architect's office
Solely the number of years since licensure
The Architect's/firm's talents, skill, experience, and imagination, and the type and level of professional services provided
A fixed government-mandated rate regardless of service type
n: Sec. 4 states compensation is based on the Architect's/firm's talents, skill, experience, imagination, and on the type and level of professional services provided. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4)

q: Under Sec. 2.1, when does an Architect render valuable input through Consultation?
o: When the Client calls on the Architect for oral or written advice, to attend conferences, or to make evaluations/appraisals — whether or not the Client pursues the project
Only if the Client eventually pursues the project
Only when a signed Owner-Architect Agreement for full services already exists
Only during the construction stage
n: Sec. 2.1 states the Architect renders valuable inputs through consultation whether or not the Client pursues the project. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.1)

q: Under Design Brief Preparation (Sec. 2.11), what does the Architect state, and for what purpose?
o: The project terms of reference (ToR), including concept, objectives, and other necessary requirements, in order to bid out architectural services (public or private)
The as-built survey of an existing structure
The final detailed cost estimate for construction
The Client's personal financial statements
n: Sec. 2.11 states the Architect prepares the project terms of reference (ToR) — concept, objectives, and other requirements — to bid out architectural services, whether public or private. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.11)

q: Pre-Feasibility Studies (Sec. 2.2) primarily rely on what kind of data, and for what purpose?
o: Researched/processed/validated secondary information (e.g., electronic, print sources), to aid the Client in early decision-making and explore readily identifiable options
Site survey data only, to compute floor area ratios
As-built data from completed comparable projects only
Primary data only, to finalize construction drawings
n: Sec. 2.2 describes Pre-Feasibility Studies as using secondary information gathered and processed to aid the Client's early decision-making and let the Client explore available/readily identifiable directions. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 2.2)

q: Using the Formula (Direct Cost = AN + CN + TN) in SPP Doc. 201, Sec. 4.1, what is the Direct Cost of this engagement?
n: AN = 40 hrs x ₱800 = ₱32,000; CN = 20 hrs x ₱1,000 = ₱20,000; TN = 60 hrs x ₱300 = ₱18,000. Direct Cost = 32,000 + 20,000 + 18,000 = ₱70,000. (Source: SPP Document 201, Sec. 4.1 (Formula: Direct Cost = AN + CN + TN))
scenario: An Architect renders Pre-Design Services (a feasibility study) for a Client under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method. The Architect logged 40 hours at ₱800/hour, one Consultant logged 20 hours at ₱1,000/hour, and Technical Staff logged 60 hours at ₱300/hour. The firm applies a multiplier of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Because the project site is 150 km from the Architect's area of operation, the Consultant and Technical Staff incurred reimbursable travel and lodging expenses totaling ₱15,000. The Client also requested 8 sets of the feasibility report instead of the standard number of copies submitted to the Client.
